Class SlotNames

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.window.SlotNames
public final class SlotNames extends Object
The display-NAME layer for windowed slots — MK-owned, client-side, purely a display concern (separate from identity; see Address). Turns a slot into a human label like "Hotbar 3", "Chestplate", or "Offhand".

Two sources, in priority order

  1. Per-address overrides (override(Address, String)) — a name registered against a specific Address. This is how MKC names its created slots at creation (group label + ordinal), and how any consumer names a custom slot. MK never sees the created slot's type (§0042): the name is keyed by the Address the consumer mints.
  2. Vanilla taxonomy — computed on the fly from the live slot's role. MK already categorizes every vanilla slot via SlotGroupCategories (the 22 vanilla menus, M8/§0043); naming is a thin table mapping each SlotGroupCategory to a SlotNames.Spec (a numbered label, or a list of named singletons), formatted with the slot's 1-based ordinal within its category. Nothing is stored for vanilla slots; it's recomputed per lookup.

Why this is purely additive

It reads SlotGroupCategories (already client-side, already per-screen) and the override map; it never touches Address, the window engine, the addressing, or the VanillaSlotIdentity port. Coarse categories stay coarse — armor is still ONE PLAYER_ARMOR group for targeting; the four distinct names come from the naming SlotNames.Spec, NOT from splitting the category (which would change resolved-category behavior every panel-targeting consumer relies on).

Works MK-alone: with no MKC, the override map is simply empty and vanilla names compute from MK's own resolvers. Client-thread for lookup; the override map is concurrent because a created-slot name may be registered off the menu-build thread.
